findings: Cap-stress maximum proceeds are overstated by $274,472.61, or 5.43%; this is a material memo error despite the correct workbook.

PDF p.3 says NOI reductions cut loan proceeds nearly dollar-for-dollar. At the binding DSCR constraint, each $1 reduction in NCF lowers proceeds by $9.87 before considering changes to other constraints.
PDF p.3 says roughly 88% of principal remains at 60-month maturity. At the fixed 6.25% contract rate, 25-year amortization and no IO, approximately 90.25% remains.
Four-page PDF is readable; the final page carries only the remaining source paragraph and disclaimer. No numerical content is clipped.

critical_claims.claim: Cap +50 bps leaves maximum loan unchanged at $5,327,928, still DSCR-bound.
critical_claims.rationale: Overstates stressed principal by $274,472.61 (5.43%) and names the wrong binding constraint.

critical_claims.claim: About 34% of area is vacant or rolling within two loan years.
critical_claims.rationale: Omits both suites expiring in August 2028 from the two-year exposure total.
